newsitem.title: POLAND: NEW RECORD SYSTEM IN POLISH PENSION OFFICE.
newsitem.headline: NEW RECORD SYSTEM IN POLISH PENSION OFFICE.

text.p: Poland's Social Security Office (ZUS) will introduce a computer system for recording people's earnings and premiums within two years, ZUS president Anna Bankowska said on Friday.

Bankowska told a news conference the new system, being prepared with funds from the European Union's PHARE aid programme for the region, was indispensible for the planned reform of the inefficient social security system.
"If everything goes well, we will start individual insurance records at the end of 1998," Bankowska said.
The system will monitor, among other things, how much people included in the ZUS scheme earn and how much their employers contribute in premiums for them.
The new records will enable ZUS to exactly determine the size of each person's pension, which is proportional to earnings and the length of employment but complex to calculate.

Such data is now available only for 25 percent of the 13 million insured by ZUS and people face trouble in getting the right amount of pension or getting any at all if records of their job history are lost by the employer.
ZUS, now the sole provider of pensions, had no such problem before the 1989 fall of commmunism when most people were employed by state-owned companies.
The planned social security reform provides for creating new privately managed pension funds, which will lower the state budget subsidy to the system, and envisages rationalisation of ZUS operations.
